newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: IOC says Sydney 2000 Games "blueprint" for future.
newsitem.headline: IOC says Sydney 2000 Games "blueprint" for future.

text.p: The International Olympic Committee on Thursday said the government financial backing and involvement in the Sydney 2000 Games was the "blueprint" for future Olympics, not the privately-backed Atlanta Games.

"There is no way the IOC will select a city that could not secure an underwriting and a good understanding between government and the private sector," said Jacques Rogge, IOC Coordination Commission chairman for the Sydney Games.
"The blueprint we see is the close association between governmental support, financially, and what I call value in kind...everything the government can offer to have good Games."

Rogge, who had just completed a routine inspection of Sydney's Games preparations, said the Sydney model was unique because a single politician had ultimate responsibility for organising the Games and building venues. In addition, the local government was also underwriting the cost of infrastructure.

The New South Wales state government has budgeted to spend A$1.91 billion (US$1.47 billion) on infrastructure, while the Games organising committee expects a A$50 million (US$38 million) profit from running the event.
The controversial Atlanta Games last year were not government-backed and Games organisers were forced to cover a US$1.7 billion budget struggled to break even.

Rogge said the problem-plagued Atlanta Olympics lacked such close government involvement, preventing the creation of a centralised chain of command to deal with transportation and communication problems.
For the first time at a Summer Olympics closing ceremony, IOC chief Juan Antonio Samaranch declined to describe the Atlanta Games as the best ever held, tagging them as "most exceptional".

"The problems in Atlanta were bad communications between the organising committe and different transport agencies. When we got into problems there was not this unified chain of command where somebody could take a decision," Rogge said.
"We have asked (future host cities) for clear and definable chain of command during Games."
